results.title: GitHub package firewall
results.author: Allison
results.content:
Editor’s note (October 21, 2026): Rewrote the changelog for clarity and added imagery.
There’s been a recent flood of malware attacks that exploit systems at package installation time. Agents and CI runners are particularly vulnerable to these attacks because they install dependencies to accomplish a task or complete a build without a human in the loop. To stem this tide, GitHub is introducing a new package firewall, which sits between endpoints or internal registries and the upstream package repositories. The firewall inspects both metadata requests and package downloads for signs of malicious activity, acting as an install-time policy gate. The package firewall is available today in public preview for all GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers, including data-resident GitHub Enterprise Cloud.
First, administrators set policy controls for their enterprise. The controls available today include a configurable cooldown period, checking the GitHub Advisory Database for malware or vulnerability advisories, and supply-chain checks like attestation downgrades.
Then, endpoints like coding agents and CI/CD hosts use the firewall for their requests instead of pointing directly at the upstream package registries. Metadata requests for package lists as well as the actual package downloads flow through the firewall, which evaluates them against the policy. If a package is blocked erroneously, the user can request an exception with a workflow similar to other GitHub Advanced Security features.
The package firewall is available in public preview as we scale up the infrastructure behind it and continue to add features based on customer demand. It is available to GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers, including GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency. The service is free while in the preview period. When it reaches general availability, it will be charged based on metered usage, similar to Actions billing.
Currently the package firewall only supports npm packages.
For detailed setup instructions, see Protecting endpoints with package firewall. Join the discussion in GitHub Community.
results.summary:
GitHub has launched a new package firewall in public preview to protect enterprise CI runners and coding agents from malicious software during the automated dependency installation process.

### Key Points
- The firewall acts as a policy gate, inspecting metadata and package downloads for malicious activity before they reach internal systems.
- Administrators can configure security controls, including cooldown periods, GitHub Advisory Database checks, and supply-chain attestation verification.
- The service is currently available to all GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers at no cost during the public preview period.
- Initial support is limited exclusively to npm packages, with plans to scale infrastructure and features based on user demand.
- Blocked packages can be appealed through an exception request workflow similar to existing GitHub Advanced Security features.

### Why it Matters
This security layer addresses critical vulnerabilities in automated build environments where human oversight is often absent during dependency installation. By centralizing policy enforcement, organizations can significantly reduce the risk of supply-chain attacks infiltrating their development pipelines.

results.title: Advanced Nuclear Fuel Strategy Weighed as Customers Seek Cost and Delivery Certainty
results.author: Edison Reed
results.content:
Gitt said diversifying nuclear fuel sources provides customers timely and cost-effective options and enables an abundant fuel solution [1]. According to him, no single fuel source checks every box and recommended a diversified fuel portfolio.
His remarks were presented in an industry perspective on diversifying nuclear fuel sources, which the cited piece says provides customers timely and cost-effective options and minimizes price and geopolitical risk [2]. The company is among five private firms selected for negotiations to receive weapons-grade plutonium under the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) Surplus Plutonium Utilization Program, according to a department announcement on May 26, 2026 [3].
Gitt said developers hope advanced nuclear plants can meet large and increasing energy needs. Data center demand has become a central driver of that interest: recent commercial deals for small modular reactors and microreactors are taking shape around a three-party model involving developers, utilities and large energy customers willing to help underwrite new projects [4].
According to the article, Gitt said a plant's fuel cost and availability can determine whether its power is too expensive or unavailable when customers need it. He said, according to the article, "You could have the best-designed plant in the world, but if its fuel costs too much or arrives too late, its power will be too expensive for customers or unavailable when they need it."
The article stated that advanced nuclear fuel differs from traditional fuel, which is typically enriched less than 5% and shaped into small oxide pellets. Advanced fuel has higher enrichment or a different form factor. Federal agencies have moved to build domestic capacity for high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU). The DOE awarded a $1.07 billion contract to a consortium led by Centrus Energy to produce HALEU, a fuel needed for advanced nuclear reactors, according to the announcement [5].
Fresh fuel made from newly mined uranium offers certainty because industry knows how to make and transport it, companies know how to buy it and regulators know how to review plants that use it, according to the article. However, it is two to three times more expensive than government-sourced or recycled fuel, the article stated.
Uranium markets have tightened alongside the interest in new reactors. Long-term uranium prices were sitting at $96 per pound, an all-time record and up about 12% year to date, according to UxC data compiled by TD Cowen [6]. Government-sourced material left over from defense, research and energy programs can be processed into advanced-reactor fuel, the article stated.
Gitt said governments spend billions to store, guard or dispose of it, but facilities for downblending and fabrication are lacking and delivery dates remain uncertain. The article's account is consistent with federal contracting activity: the Department of Energy has committed $2.7 billion over the next decade to three companies – Centrus Energy, Orano Federal Services and General Matter – to develop domestic uranium enrichment capabilities and reduce reliance on Russian-supplied nuclear fuel [7].
Recycled fuel is described as the strongest long-term option. An article on Real Clear Energy stated that most current reactors use about 5% of fuel energy, leaving 95% behind, and that recycling could cut fuel costs by as much as 80%. The article also stated that recycled fuel requires commercial-scale recycling facilities, that not all advanced reactors can run on it, and that the system cannot be built overnight.
Federal support for the concept has been limited in scale so far: The DOE awarded $2.5 million to Curio, a nuclear technology company, to advance the recycling of spent nuclear fuel, with the project targeting the processing of 4,000 tons of used fuel using a chemical separation method [8]. The article's description of spent fuel as an energy resource is echoed in industry commentary holding that spent fuel retains over 90% of its energy potential [9].
Gitt compared a diversified fuel portfolio to not putting all retirement savings into a single stock, saying a bad outcome in one sector should not threaten the entire plan. The diversification principle is a familiar one in long-term planning. A Kazakhstani policy review recommended restructuring administration of private pension savings while changing investment rules to allow for portfolio diversification [10].
Gitt said using fresh fuel, government material and recycled fuel together can reduce supply risk, control costs and help scale advanced nuclear power faster than any single source. The article stated that fresh fuel offers the most certain near-term path, government material can provide a lower-cost middle-term option and recycled fuel offers long-term scale and economics.
Gitt said traditional light-water reactors should remain part of the mix. The article stated that about 93% of uranium purchased by U.S. nuclear plant operators in 2025 came from foreign sources.
The supply-chain concern has been documented elsewhere: the nation's nuclear energy ambitions face severe fuel supply chain vulnerabilities, including dependence on Russian uranium [11]. Gitt said diversifying nuclear fuel sources provides customers timely and cost-effective options, turns waste and government material into assets and minimizes price and geopolitical risk.
results.summary:
Industry experts are advocating for a diversified nuclear fuel portfolio, combining fresh uranium, government-sourced materials, and recycled fuel to stabilize costs and secure supply chains for advanced reactors.

### Key Points
- The U.S. Department of Energy has committed $2.7 billion to Centrus Energy, Orano Federal Services, and General Matter to develop domestic uranium enrichment capabilities.
- Centrus Energy received a $1.07 billion contract to produce high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU), a critical fuel source for next-generation advanced nuclear reactors.
- Long-term uranium prices reached a record $96 per pound, reflecting a 12% year-to-date increase driven by tightening global markets and rising demand.
- Recycling spent nuclear fuel could potentially reduce fuel costs by up to 80%, as current reactors utilize only about 5% of available fuel energy.
- The Department of Energy awarded $2.5 million to Curio to develop chemical separation methods for processing 4,000 tons of spent nuclear fuel.

### Why it Matters
Diversifying fuel sources is essential for mitigating geopolitical risks and reducing heavy reliance on foreign uranium, which accounted for 93% of U.S. purchases in 2025. By integrating recycled and government-sourced materials, the industry aims to lower costs and ensure the reliable energy supply required to meet the growing power demands of modern data centers.

results.title: "AI is a technofascist, anti-human and anti-art project", says creator of lefty tech satire Future? No Thanks!, before explaining why he used it anyway
results.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
results.content:
Prominent capital-p Political game developer and left-wing academic Paulo "Molleindustria" Pedercini has revealed that he used generative AI tools for aspects of recent ecosocialist satire Future? No Thanks!. According to Pedercini, "a tiny fraction of its code was written with AI support" towards the end of the project, specifically to assess and fix bugs.
The game also uses text-to-speech voice-acting for a couple of characters, generated with ElevenLab software, with Pedercini noting that the characters in question are intended as a spoof of wonky artificial intelligence. He insists that none of the game's art or writing is AI-generated. These insights arrive weeks after the game's Steam release, which was delayed due to Valve's concerns about sexual material. Back then, there was no genAI disclosure on the game's storepage. There is one now.
Pedercini fessed up about using generative AI on his blog yesterday. "Every independent gaming festival and showcase in the year 2026 requires some kind of generative AI disclosure," he begins. "That is great! Slop and vibe-coded games are a scourge, AI is a technofascist, anti-human and anti-art project, and it’s imperative to create spaces of resistance.
"Future? No Thanks! is a game that tackles the impact and limits of artificial intelligence head-on," Pedercini continues. "It satirizes generative AI and the careless ways it can be used, even in an enlightened ecosocialist world. It also dramatizes beneficial uses, such as coordinating a planned economy, voice recognition, and talking robots. And yet, I can’t say it’s a 100% AI free game."
In a breakdown of development of Future! No Thanks, stretching back to 2021, Pedercini comments that "99% of its code base was written before AI was even viable as a coding tool". As for why he decided to use it during the closing stages, he argues that "ChatGPT or Claude" can be "a powerful semantic search engine" when fixing bugs.
"Search engines have been enshittified to death, specific technical queries don’t yield meaningful results anymore," Pedercini writes. "Most search engines produce low quality AI responses anyway. Such coding assistance was used for things like fixing a shader I didn’t write which broke after an update, or diagnosing a one-frame loading glitch when loading sequences. Finishing touches and minor debugging.
"Unlike assets that can be easily swapped, AI generated code is hard to remove once introduced," he goes on. "I wouldn’t be able to tell which lines I wrote, which were generated, and which were somewhere in between."
Regarding the game's voicework, Pedercini argues that "text-to-speech used to be an uncontroversial technology and an early application of neural networks. Then the AI bros started commercializing AI voices as a way to replace human actors, so it’s now problematic."
Apparently, Future? No Thanks! features "about two minutes" of generated voicework "for an automated toilet and a personal assistant that mis-translates Roman idioms". Pedercini spells out that "the humor of these scenes relies on uncanny voices doing their job poorly". The Future? No Thanks! team experimented with human voices for these roles, he adds, but found "they just weren’t working as well". He includes a clip of the PA character for reference.
Early demos of the game also featured some AI-generated "fake doo-woop tunes" with "AI" in the lyrics that "were supposed to make fun of losers who listen to slop". The referencing of AI in the lyrics was "conceived as a kind of mandatory watermark this future society imposes to AI-generated music," Pedercini explains. "I thought they were hilarious, but over time the association with a plagiarist tech company started to bother me so I replaced them with royalty free loops. By the way, royalty free samples that are certainly AI-free are increasingly hard to find, but I found an old site untouched since 2016."
Pedercini ends his blog (as of writing, anyway) with some thoughts on discussion around generative AI in games, commenting that the "100% no-AI stance/requirement" adopted by a fair few devs and players "is very recent, and the game was being developed before a consensus emerged". He adds that "as an educator I have to look into these tools which most of my students use, and I was trying to figure out if there are non-brain-rotting ways to do so. I’m grateful to those who allow some nuance in approaching the issue, especially regarding coding."
An older version of the blog had some lengthier thoughts about genAI, in which Pedercini argued that being "AI-free" is "the only truly ethical position" for game developers, given the technology's association with "energy and water use, IP theft, cheating, unemployment, spam, and so on". Nonetheless, he contended that genAI's evils reflect larger structural problems that can't be remedied through individual action, while arguing that "holding your fellow artists to the highest ethical standards won't stop the actual bad actors", and that enforcing "AI-free" within a "progressively minded community" may come at "a high cost of division, suspicion, and bad vibes".
These closing thoughts have now been deleted following some vehement responses on Bluesky, with Pedercini now commenting that they "made people upset and made me a strawman for arguments and positions I abhor". You can still find screen caps of the removed paragraphs in the wilds.
I like what I've played of Future! No Thanks?, and this is obviously a more "nuanced" injection of stochastic parrotry than the bazillions of quick cash-in games that consist purely of 'human-reviewed' generated code, or the blockbuster projects that are jamming it in at the behest of investors and executives. I broadly agree with Pedercini that generative AI is just the freshest wart on the arse of a callous social order that puts economic growth above everything else. I respect the intention to use the technology in the service of a story or theme, and I hear the point about certain, hitherto less damaging machine learning technologies being absorbed into the genAI crusade. And sure, people do like to tell each other off on social media, don't they?
That said, I find all this pretty disappointing. Given Pedercini's clear understanding of all the problems with generative AI, and given that Future? No Thanks! itself offers criticism of the tech, the least you'd expect is that he'd make his case for using the stuff in advance of selling the game. It would be a show of good faith. Pedercini also doesn't specify whether he sought out genAI tools that aren't as steeped in infamy as Claude, ChatGPT and Suno.
While I don't want to lean too much on commentary that has now been withdrawn, I also think Pedercini sets up too hard a binary between "individual action" and "structural problems" in the older version of the post. I agree that harping about "personal responsibility" is one of the weapons capitalism deploys to pit its discontents against each other, but a community that wants to create "spaces of resistance" against "a technofascist, anti-human and anti-art project" needs to hold members to an appropriate standard.
A number of other devs have responded to Pedercini's blog, including Necrobarista and Eternal Strands writer Damon Reece and Riot Games IP creative adviser Dante Douglas, who is also narrative lead on Airborne Empire. I imagine Pedercini will have more to say soon.
Read this next
- "I'm desperately looking for anybody who knows anybody at Valve": open world satire Future? No Thanks! is still locked in Steam horny jail
- Indie open worlder Future? No Thanks! gets last minute delay after Steam content mods allegedly demand a "watch the sex scene" button
- "Enjoy your last day in a future that works for everyone but you": I adore the demo for Future? No Thanks, an open world comedy about a boomer trapped in leftwing paradise
results.summary:
Game developer Paulo Pedercini has disclosed the use of generative AI tools for debugging and voice acting in his ecosocialist satire game, Future? No Thanks!.

### Key Points
- Paulo Pedercini used ChatGPT and Claude to assist with minor code debugging during the final stages of development.
- The game features approximately two minutes of AI-generated voice acting via ElevenLabs for characters intended to parody artificial intelligence.
- Pedercini previously removed AI-generated music from the game due to concerns regarding the technology's association with copyright infringement.
- A generative AI disclosure has been added to the game's Steam store page following the developer's public admission.
- Development of the project began in 2021, with the developer stating that 99% of the codebase was written without AI assistance.

### Why it Matters
This disclosure highlights the growing tension between independent developers and the evolving ethical standards regarding AI usage in creative projects. It underscores the difficulty of maintaining a strictly "AI-free" development process while navigating the practical limitations of modern software tools and community expectations.

results.title: Tesla-SpaceX Merger Being Considered
results.author: BeauHD
results.content:
Elon Musk says a merger between Tesla and SpaceX is under active consideration, with special committees at both companies evaluating a deal that could combine businesses valued at roughly $3.5 trillion. "Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes," Musk said during a call with financial analysts over the quarterly business results of SpaceX on Tuesday. The BBC reports:  While Musk noted the certainty of such a merger should not be assumed, and it would need shareholders' support, he said special committees within both companies have been formed to examine the move. "The special committees have not reached agreement on terms of any transaction and there's no guarantee that they will," Musk added. "But I do think there is a lot of merit to merging and a lot to be gained."
[...] The company, which builds space rockets and Starlink internet satellites, is now expanding into offering cloud compute capacity for other tech companies, like Anthropic and Google. That line of business has become the most profitable part of SpaceX, bringing in $7.5bn according to the latest quarterly results (PDF). Starlink also tallied revenue of $5.2bn. SpaceX as a whole, however, is not profitable and has lost $1.1bn so far this year.
[...] Musk said on Tuesday a full merger between the two companies would make sense for the work each is doing around chips, artificial intelligence, software and more. He described himself as a "conflicted party" as the chief executive of Tesla and of SpaceX. Even commenting on the possibility of a merger between the two companies, Musk compared to "tap dancing through a minefield." He added a merger would ultimately be decided by shareholders. At least 50% of Tesla's shareholders would need to approve the merger, which Musk described as "quite a high hurdle to achieve."
results.summary:
Elon Musk has confirmed that special committees at Tesla and SpaceX are actively evaluating a potential merger that could combine two companies with a combined $3.5 trillion valuation.

### Key Points
- Elon Musk stated that special committees at both companies are currently examining the feasibility of a potential merger.
- A successful deal would require approval from at least 50% of Tesla shareholders, a threshold Musk described as a significant hurdle.
- SpaceX reported $7.5 billion in revenue from its cloud computing division and $5.2 billion from Starlink, despite an overall year-to-date loss of $1.1 billion.
- Musk cited potential synergies in artificial intelligence, software development, and chip technology as primary motivations for combining the two entities.
- No formal agreement on transaction terms has been reached, and Musk emphasized that there is no guarantee a merger will proceed.

### Why it Matters
A merger between these two industry giants would create a massive, vertically integrated conglomerate spanning automotive, aerospace, and artificial intelligence sectors. This consolidation could fundamentally reshape the tech and energy markets, though it faces significant regulatory scrutiny and shareholder approval challenges.

results.title: Live updates: Bitcoin clings to $82,500 as SpaceX results lift stock futures
results.author: Shaurya Malwa
results.content:
Bitcoin is hanging just above $82,500 on Wednesday, the level XS.com’s Simon-Peter Massabni calls its most important support, as stock futures climbed on SpaceX’s blowout results and oil pushed back above $110.
Bitcoin’s fate is tied to tech again. It fell in lockstep with the Nasdaq last week after the hot U.S. inflation report and a selloff in AI and chip stocks, and Massabni, XS.com’s head of business development, said that link is getting stronger.
“In the short term, this development challenges the notion that Bitcoin can consistently serve as an independent safe haven from traditional market volatility,” he said.
A “decisive and sustained break” below $82,500 could hand control to sellers and expose bitcoin to a drop toward $70,000, Massabni said. That’s the downside case laid out by market maker Wintermute, and it would mean a further 15% slide from here.
Tech gave bitcoin some cover on Wednesday. 
Nasdaq 100 futures rose 0.4% and S&P 500 futures 0.2%. SpaceX jumped 9% before the open after its AI and satellite internet businesses drove earnings well above forecasts, and a report that Anthropic may spend $750 billion on computing power eased worries about the AI spending boom. 
Brent topped $110 a barrel on attacks near the Strait of Hormuz, and Treasury yields edged higher. Meta and Tesla report later Wednesday.
A move back above $84,000 would take the $70,000 scenario off the table.
results.summary:
Bitcoin remains precariously positioned above the critical $82,500 support level as the cryptocurrency’s price continues to track closely with broader volatility in the technology sector and stock markets.

### Key Points
- Bitcoin is currently trading just above $82,500, a threshold analysts identify as a vital support level to prevent a potential slide toward $70,000.
- Market maker Wintermute warns that a sustained break below the current support could trigger a 15% decline in the asset's value.
- SpaceX shares rose 9% in pre-market trading following strong earnings results from its artificial intelligence and satellite internet divisions.
- Nasdaq 100 futures climbed 0.4% as reports of significant computing power investments by Anthropic helped stabilize investor sentiment regarding the AI sector.
- Brent crude oil prices surpassed $110 per barrel following reports of regional attacks near the Strait of Hormuz.

### Why it Matters
The strengthening correlation between Bitcoin and tech stocks challenges the narrative that the cryptocurrency functions as an independent safe haven during periods of market instability. Investors are closely monitoring these price levels to determine if Bitcoin will maintain its current valuation or face a deeper correction tied to broader macroeconomic trends.

results.title: Nvidia reveals plans to build AI data centers in 14 days instead of 6 months
results.author: Daniel Howley
results.content:
Nvidia reveals plans for 'an AI factory in a shipping container' to build data centers in weeks, not months
Nvidia (NVDA) wants to reduce the time it takes for its customers to start generating revenue from its AI systems.
At its GTC event in Berlin on Wednesday, the company unveiled its DSX POD, a reference design for an AI data center packed into a box about the size of a standard shipping container.
Data center construction can take months, if not years, to get up and running. And because they don't start generating revenue until they begin processing AI tokens, the longer a data center takes to come online, the more expenses pile up.
The DSX POD is meant to serve as a faster, modular solution for companies that need access to data center capabilities sooner rather than later.
"The moment then you have to install these AI factories, and they're gigantic. And putting these AI factories into service takes months. If we could reduce that months, you know, from the moment that the systems are shipped to the moment that it's deployed and being operational, if we could reduce it from months to weeks or even a month, that will be completely game-changing for all of these AI factories," CEO Jensen Huang told Deirdre Bosa.
According to Nvidia, the Vera Rubin-powered DSX PODs will arrive on site, ready to be plugged into the power, cooling, and networking infrastructure, reducing deployment time from six months to 14 days.
The company said DSX PODs won't replace traditional data centers, but will serve as a means to start running AI applications before brick-and-mortar facilities are ready.
"With Nvidia DSX POD, we're bringing factory-built precision and speed to AI infrastructure construction — reducing deployment time from months to weeks so customers can scale capacity and bring revenue-generating production online faster," Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said in a statement.
According to the company, the DSX POD supports liquid cooling, but because it uses dry-cooler designs, it can save up to 54 million liters of water per day versus a standard data center.
Standing up data centers more quickly doesn't just help Nvidia's customers, though. Faster data center deployment should ease at least one of the chokepoints in the AI build-out, which means faster chip sales for Nvidia.
Semiconductors aren't the only bottleneck for data center builders. Getting the electricity necessary to power those processors is also a concern. And power plants take far longer to construct than data centers.
Nvidia said it's working with partners, including Anduril, Armada, Bull, Crusoe, Dell Technologies (DELL), Foxconn, and others, to begin delivering the DSX POD in early 2027.
Email Daniel Howley at dhowley@yahoofinance.com. Follow him on Twitter at @DanielHowley.
results.summary:
Nvidia unveiled its DSX POD reference design, a modular, shipping-container-sized data center solution engineered to reduce infrastructure deployment times from six months to just 14 days.

### Key Points
- The DSX POD is a pre-built, modular AI data center designed to be operational within two weeks of arrival.
- Nvidia claims the system utilizes dry-cooler designs, potentially saving up to 54 million liters of water daily compared to traditional facilities.
- The units are powered by Vera Rubin architecture and are intended to supplement, rather than replace, permanent brick-and-mortar data centers.
- Nvidia is collaborating with partners including Dell Technologies, Foxconn, Anduril, and Armada to begin deliveries in early 2027.

### Why it Matters
This modular approach addresses a critical bottleneck in the AI industry by allowing companies to begin generating revenue while waiting for permanent data center construction. By accelerating deployment, Nvidia can increase its own chip sales while helping customers scale their AI infrastructure more efficiently.

results.title: iPhone Duo Is Delightful, and Different
results.author: Josh Rubin
results.content:
After a week with iPhone Duo, I’m pleased that Apple‘s first foldable can work as both a pocketable phone and a small tablet without compromising either. The 5.4-inch outer screen handles glances and quick maneuvers on the move and the 7.6-inch inner display opens for anything that deserves focus—a rhythm that has changed how and where I use a phone. The battery outlasts expectations and the hinge feels precise in its resistance, considered in its form and deeply satisfying to close. Years of iPhone muscle memory took a few days to yield, and some trade-offs, from the return to Touch ID to an incompatible MagSafe wallet, temper the delight without undoing it. Personally, the Duo also closes a loop that opened in 1999.
That year, my graduate thesis at ITP, NYU’s Interactive Telecommunications Program, was the conceptual design and interface prototyping of a future looking four-screen folding phone that Kent Hollrah and I called The Stack. It studied form setting function, with one configuration for reading, another for calls and another for maps, as much as it explored how software should behave on hardware that changes shape. Kent and I got a lot wrong in our forecast and a few things right, and it’s gratifying to see questions we once sketched answered, with far more finesse, in how the Duo’s postures shape its uses. I’ve tested many foldables over the years since they first came to market, but as someone embedded in the Apple ecosystem, this is the first I’ve been able to truly bring into daily life. It has also pared down what I carry. Until now I often traveled with an iPhone Pro alongside an iPad mini, the Duo now covers both. That hardly makes it an iPad killer, since there are still many tasks for which an iPad, especially one of the larger models, remains the best device.
The most surprising usage change is behavioral. Closed, the Duo is ideal for pruning an inbox with a thumb and firing off a terse response or, better, dictating one to Siri. When managing email requires more attention, opening the phone puts a message and the inbox side by side. That division of labor has spread beyond Mail. The outer screen is small enough to discourage lingering, so on the street I check, answer and pocket, saving the inner display for whenever I’m still, whether at a desk, on a sofa, at a café table or simply standing in place. The result is screen time with greater intentionality, and I feel more in control of when I let myself get pulled into a deep scroll. The open screen serves more than consumption, obviously. Making things, from photographing and editing images to writing, is far better on the larger canvas, and so is a round of Crossplay. The Stack argued that a device’s shape could direct its purpose, and it’s rewarding to watch that idea work as a behavioral nudge.
The initial delight of opening the Duo has settled into a quiet confidence, and its hinge now sets the bar for how every hinge should feel. Built from more than 100 components, it moves through its arc with measured tension, closer to a well-made notebook than a mechanism. Both displays share a 1.4:1 aspect ratio, so content scales up mid-task or reflows into a new layout if appropriate, and that continuity is the Duo’s most consequential design choice precisely because it goes unnoticed. A micro-blasted, 3D-printed titanium hinge cover contrasts with the mirror-polished Grade 5 titanium frame, making the spine read as a deliberate architectural element. Closed, it has the proportions of a passport and pockets as easily.
Foldability invites postures a slab phone can’t hold. Bent like a laptop, the Duo becomes a natural setup for watching videos of for FaceTime, its camera hidden beneath the inner display until needed, and a handy stand for shooting photos.
StandBy, which turns a docked iPhone into an ambient clock and widget display, no longer needs a charger on the Duo, and I’ve used it in every configuration. Fully open on a charger at my desk, it becomes nearly a home dashboard, pairing two small widgets and a large one on the left with an extra-large widget on the right. Partially folded and stood like a book, the inner display does the same without a cable. Tented into an inverted V, the outer screen offers clock, photo, modular, weather and calendar faces, and a Wake Up alarm in that position brings a glow that slowly brightens across the inner display.
Laid open and flat on a table, the Duo rocks on its camera plateau, a problem Apple’s Folio with Kickstand, designed for upright, angled viewing, doesn’t solve. Somebody will likely design an accessory that levels it. In the meantime, I’ve been sliding my phone tatami mat under the upper half, which tilts the screen to a pleasant angle and ends the wobble.
Sound remains consistent regardless of form. Because the distance between the speakers changes as the Duo opens, folds and rotates, Apple compensates with real-time tuning, and whether the phone is tented, propped or held open, audio never lurches with a change of position. Apple says the microphones are likewise placed for each configuration, though I haven’t heard a Duo call from the other end.
Two screens haven’t taken a toll on battery. A cell in each half, with power managed by custom silicon, behaves as a single battery, and Apple claims up to 44 hours of video playback on the outer display versus 31 on the inner. On a full day running around the city, I carried a charger out of habit and never needed it, a genuine shift for someone used to topping up daily. A breakdown in Settings showing drain by display or folded state (this is a feature request) would make the trade-off between modes legible rather than intuited.
Moving from a conventional iPhone is where the Duo demands extra attention. The software looks as familiar as ever, but on the Duo, controls that have long lived along the top and bottom of the screen migrate to the side, so several interactions require relearning. Dynamic Island, the pill-shaped home for live alerts around the front camera, sits in a vertical rail along the right edge and pushes interface elements down, so in apps like Messages the back button doesn’t always land in the same place. Control Center screens are shorter, and after migration the last two rows of my layout spilled onto a new page. Neither issue is serious, and the adjustment has largely passed, though I still occasionally pause to recall where something lives. The clearest sign came when I picked up my 18 Pro after days of deliberately avoiding it, and the conventional phone was the one that felt foreign, and strikingly tall.
Authentication takes recalibration too. The Duo trades Face ID for Touch ID in the side button, so the first step is enrolling several fingers. I registered both index fingers and my right thumb, because the screen reorients to however the phone is held and the button lands somewhere different each time I seem to need it. Unlocking with Apple Watch shortens the path, with one quirk: holding the phone while it’s inside a pocket can unlock the phone, and more than once a tap on my wrist was the first sign the Duo had woken and was pocket-dial-ready. Apple Pay is slower, since double-clicking and confirming with a fingerprint can’t match Face ID’s glance at a checkout counter. MagSafe wallets won’t attach because of the Duo’s size and shape, which stings for anyone who consolidated cards onto the back of their phone—I’ve had to get used to carrying a separate wallet again. I also miss the Action Button, which I had mapped to Gemini for quick lookups; Gemini answers those faster than Siri, whose handoff to an outside chatbot is limited to ChatGPT.
Two displays, four cameras and a hinge that holds whatever angle it’s given open up shooting scenarios a slab phone can’t. Unfolded, the outer screen faces the subject. Duo Preview shows people a live view of themselves while framing them with the rear cameras, so they can adjust their pose without waiting for direction. Kid Cue plays Snoopy animations there to draw a child’s gaze to the lens; turns out it makes adults smile too. Turned around, the same arrangement makes selfies with the 48MP rear cameras practical, framed on the outer screen rather than guessed at, provided you look at the lenses rather than the preview once the shot is framed, or your sightline drifts. Propped on a table, the Duo becomes its own photographer: Smart Take uses on-device models to release the shutter once everyone is posed, retiring the sprint back from a self-timer. Dual Capture records the front and rear cameras at once, and Duo FaceTime lets someone beside you join a video call through the outer display and camera, so nobody has to crowd around one screen.
The Duo’s camera system isn’t the 18 Pro’s equal. Both models share the 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide, Cinematic focus effects applied after capture and the new texture and grain controls in Photographic Styles are a joy to find here. The Duo’s 48MP Fusion main camera can default to 26, 28 or 35 mm and reaches 2x the same way the 18 Pro does, but without the Pro’s dedicated telephoto, the 4x and 8x options are missing. The mechanical variable aperture and manual Pro controls are exclusive to the 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max.
That gap is where iPhone Handoff earns its place. The iOS 27 feature moves one phone number to whichever of two iPhones is unlocked, and with T-Mobile it has carried mine between the Duo and the 18 Pro seamlessly. The Duo handles daily life, from reading and writing to triage and calls to casual photography, while the 18 Pro stays at the ready for situations that call for more camera control. The two meet in iCloud Photos, where shots from the Pro arrive on the Duo, which has power to spare for editing and, unfolded, makes a finer darkroom than any slab.
iPhone Duo arrives 23 October 2026 at $1,999 for the 256GB configuration, in Night Sky and Star White. It asks its owner to unlearn a few habits and accept a few compromises, and repays both with a phone that stays small when life is in motion, opens into a canvas when it isn’t and, for anyone who has imagined such a device for decades, offers the pleasure of finally carrying one.
results.summary:
The new Apple iPhone Duo, a foldable device featuring a 5.4-inch outer screen and 7.6-inch inner display, launches on October 23, 2026, with a starting price of $1,999.

### Key Points
- The device features a precision-engineered titanium hinge and dual-display architecture designed for seamless content scaling.
- It replaces Face ID with side-button Touch ID and requires users to adapt to new interface layouts and navigation controls.
- Camera capabilities include Duo Preview and Smart Take, though it lacks the dedicated telephoto lens found on the iPhone 18 Pro.
- Battery life is managed by custom silicon across two internal cells, supporting extended use without requiring mid-day charging.
- The phone is available in Night Sky and Star White colorways, starting at a 256GB storage capacity.

### Why it Matters
The iPhone Duo represents Apple’s first entry into the foldable market, signaling a shift in how the company balances hardware form factors with user behavior. By offering a device that functions as both a compact phone and a tablet, Apple is challenging the dominance of traditional slab-style smartphones while testing consumer willingness to accept specific trade-offs in exchange for increased screen versatility.

results.title: Apple Could Owe Even More After $5.7 Billion Patent Verdict
results.author: Hartley Charlton
results.content:
Apple could face additional payments on top of a $5.7 billion patent verdict, with Taction Technology asking a federal judge for more damages, interest, and royalties on future iPhone and Apple Watch sales.
The request follows a September jury verdict that Apple's Taptic Engine infringed two Taction patents covering haptic feedback, the technology that produces taps and vibrations in devices. Apple disputes the verdict and is seeking to have it overturned or obtain a new trial.
According to Reuters, Taction says the $5.7 billion award covers sales from 2021 through to late March 2026. It now wants compensation for approximately six more months of sales that were not included in the jury's initial calculation.
Taction is also asking for interest on the damages at an annual rate of 7%, citing California law. That could increase the amount by hundreds of millions of dollars. Separately, it wants interest to continue accumulating after the court enters its final judgment until Apple pays.
The company's request also extends to future sales. Taction wants Apple to pay royalties on devices using the disputed technology until the patents expire on September 24, 2035. Under its proposal, Apple would report U.S. sales every quarter and pay within 30 days of the quarter ending.
Moreover, Taction argues that newer models, including the iPhone 18 Pro and Apple Watch Series 12, should also be covered because their relevant technology has not changed enough to escape the patent claims. To support that position, it points to Apple's earlier litigation against Samsung, in which Apple argued that royalties should extend to newer products with essentially the same infringing technology.
Apple maintains that its Taptic Engine is fundamentally different from Taction's technology. It has also challenged the size of the jury's award, arguing that the evidence did not support the $5.7 billion calculation, and has said it will appeal.
results.summary:
Taction Technology is seeking additional damages, interest, and ongoing royalties from Apple following a $5.7 billion jury verdict regarding patent infringement in the company's Taptic Engine technology.

### Key Points
- A federal jury previously found Apple’s Taptic Engine infringed on two patents held by Taction Technology.
- Taction is requesting compensation for an additional six months of sales not covered in the original $5.7 billion award.
- The company seeks a 7% annual interest rate on damages, potentially adding hundreds of millions to the total payout.
- Taction wants ongoing royalties on future iPhone and Apple Watch sales until its patents expire in September 2035.
- Apple disputes the verdict, arguing its technology is distinct, and is currently seeking a new trial or a reversal of the judgment.

### Why it Matters
This legal dispute highlights the significant financial risks major tech companies face regarding intellectual property and haptic feedback components. If the court grants Taction's request for ongoing royalties, it could establish a long-term financial burden for Apple's future hardware releases.

results.title: Android 17 beta tackles a security loophole thieves could exploit
results.author: techkritiko@gmail.com (Jay Bonggolto) , Jay Bonggolto
results.content:
What you need to know
- Android 17 QPR3 Beta 2 has added a toggle to require PIN/fingerprint authentication before anyone can touch Airplane Mode, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or Mobile Data on a locked phone.
- Non-security tiles like Flashlight, Auto-rotate, and Battery Saver stay unlocked and accessible without extra friction.
- The latest Android 17 beta release also resolves random reboots, system crashes, Bluetooth pairing failures, idle battery drain, and buggy internet tiles.
Google is finally giving Pixel owners a way to stop thieves from disabling their phone’s connectivity right from the lock screen.
The new security feature is coming in Android 17 QPR3 Beta 2, which will let users require authentication before anyone can toggle Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, mobile data, or airplane mode. It's a small change, but it could make a stolen phone a little less useful to whoever walks away with it.
This update, which came on October 20 with build number DP11.261002.005, does more than just fix a number of bugs. The Android Beta team says on Reddit that it also fixes intermittent device crashes and unexpected reboots, Bluetooth pairing failures, excessive idle battery drain, and issues with the Internet Quick Settings tile. Below is the complete list of issues fixed in the latest beta round.
- Devices intermittently crash and reboot during normal use. (Issue #570031572, Issue #570031155, Issue #569529428, Issue #569222433, Issue #570414567, Issue #570725957, Issue #569237164, Issue #572493638)
- Internet Quick Settings tile displays persistent text when mobile data is active without Wi-Fi. (Issue #354469154, Issue #367059437)
- Media output dialog ignores the monochrome system theme when external audio devices are connected. (Issue #476304142)
- Pin icon glitches position next to pinned apps in the share sheet. (Issue #476234992)
- Internal PublishedApi declarations trigger unexpected API lint and source compatibility check errors. (Issue #562178518)
- Device unexpectedly shuts down during WhatsApp video calls. (Issue #554451749, Issue #559966303)
- Lock screen in-progress notifications overlap with other UI elements and cause stuttering panel animations. (Issue #547371609, Issue #548539836, Issue #562186670)
- Cellular data, MMS, and hotspot services fail to connect on Dish Network. (Issue #537736046)
- Screen recording freezes and stops capturing frames after screen rotation. (Issue #541325203)
- System UI, fonts, and apps render at an abnormally small scale regardless of configured display size settings. (Issue #563321433)
- Display turns black and becomes unresponsive after ending a phone call. (Issue #564953545)
- Terminal app fails to launch the Linux development environment virtual machine after installation. (Issue #551657934)
- Wi-Fi Aware fails to establish subsequent data paths with a no interfaces available error after releasing an accept-any responder network request during connection confirmation. (Issue #550726291)
- Paired watch continues to ring after an incoming call is answered on the phone. (Issue #564594780)
- Airbnb app fails to connect when attempting to send messages. (Issue #563024453)
- Quick Settings Bluetooth subtitle is misaligned to the right. (Issue #559417120)
- App drawer unexpectedly closes when switching keyboard language. (Issue #558774933, Issue #540389222, Issue #533125590)
- Bluetooth pairing fails due to a connection timeout when attempting to pair with a device. (Issue #563675080)
- VoLTE, VoNR, and Wi-Fi calling are unavailable on the IT&E network. (Issue #556432987)
- High idle battery drain caused by motion sensors remaining active after using Face Unlock or the camera. (Issue #568078965)
- Wi-Fi Calling unavailable on the OXIO network. (Issue #563089593)
A more interesting addition is the connectivity restriction, as noted in a few replies to the Reddit post. Sometimes thieves can disable a phone’s network connections from the lock screen, making it more difficult for owners to track down a lost device. It’s another hurdle to force you to unlock before changing these settings, though it obviously won’t prevent all theft or ensure recovery.
To enable it, go to Settings > Security & privacy > Device unlock or Settings > Display & touch > Lock screen, then turn Lock Quick Settings connectivity on. Once enabled, you must unlock the device before you can change any of the four protected connectivity settings.
Google is also leaving common shortcuts like flashlight, auto-rotate, and Battery Saver accessible, so the security feature doesn’t relegate the lock screen to a glorified clock. Locking each and every Quick Settings tile would be way too limiting for those who enjoy shortcuts without unlocking their phone. So it’s a more targeted way to protect the settings that could interfere with connectivity and tracking.
Android 17 QPR3 Beta 2 is available for eligible Pixel devices enrolled in Google’s Android Beta Program. As with any beta software, users should expect the possibility of bugs and avoid installing on a device they can’t afford to have misbehave.
